title: Calculate Total Revenue
description: You're analyzing an e-commerce store's sales data. Every line item in `order_items` records a `quantity` and a `unit_price` at the time of purchase. Write a query that returns the store's total revenue as `total_revenue` - the sum of quantity times unit_price across every order item.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: SUM, computed expressions
Revenue per line item is quantity * unit_price - SUM() adds that expression up across every row in order_items, not just one column.
Select SUM of (quantity times unit_price), aliased as total_revenue, from order_items.
expected_behavior: Returns one row, one column (total_revenue), the sum of quantity * unit_price across all order_items.
solution: SELECT SUM(quantity * unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM order_items;
explanation: This is the same SUM-of-a-computed-expression pattern from Foundations, applied to a real business question - revenue isn't a stored column anywhere, it's derived from quantity and unit_price at query time.
